title: CoT-Evo: Evolutionary Distillation of Chain-of-Thought for Scientific Reasoning
claim: A multi-stage system builds a diverse pool, selects by novelty and fitness, recombines and mutates, and loops iteratively to evolve high-quality outputs.
layout: 4 labeled panels (a–d): two side-by-side on top, a wide panel in the middle, and a bottom loop strip; mostly left-to-right and top-to-bottom with arrows
description: A four-panel diagram of an evolutionary CoT distillation framework. Panel a (top left) shows Question and Answer boxes feeding two stages: CoT generation by several LLM logos with prompt strategies (chain, backward, tree of thought drawn as node chains), and knowledge augmentation that produces knowledge-snippet cards. Together they form an Initial Candidate Pool, drawn as a row of colored DNA helices. Panel b (top right) takes that pool through a behavioral embedding, a K-nearest-neighbor novelty score and a fitness function (colored dots with criteria). It combines them into a local competition score and a Pareto-based selection of parent candidates. Panel c (middle) shows recombination of a target CoT with a strategy provider, and three mutation operators (add, delete, innovate) that produce offspring trajectories. Panel d (bottom) is a simple loop of four colored boxes. Pastel color-coded boxes and icons are used throughout.
caption: Overview of COT-EVO. (a) Multi-thinker CoT initialization constructs a diverse pool of candidates. (b) Novelty-driven candidate selection evaluates them via a composite fitness function and retains promising trajectories. (c) Reflective recombination and mutation generate new offspring CoTs through targeted operations. (d) These modules form the iterative COT-EVO optimization loop, which evolves compact, accurate, and domain-reliable CoTs for downstream training.
abstract: While chain-of-thought (CoT) distillation from advanced large language models (LLMs) has proven effective in general reasoning tasks, it struggles in scientific domains where even advanced models often produce incorrect or superficial reasoning due to high complexity and specialized knowledge requirements. Directly distilling from such flawed outputs results in low-quality training data and limits the performance of smaller student models. To overcome this, we propose CoT-Evo, an evolutionary CoT distillation framework. It begins by constructing a diverse pool of reasoning trajectories from multiple LLM thinkers, enriches them with automatically retrieved domain knowledge, and iteratively refines the trajectories using novelty-driven selection, reflective recombination and mutation. The refinement is guided by a fitness function that evaluates answer correctness, coherence, and effective knowledge utilization. This results in a high-quality CoT dataset tailored for scientific reasoning. We employ this evolved dataset to fine-tune a compact model, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on scientific reasoning benchmarks. Our work establishes a scalable approach to synthesizing high-fidelity scientific reasoning data from diverse and fallible LLMs.
